mcp/uk-rates.instructions: Current UK tax-year rates and thresholds from databutler.dev, each verified against gov.uk and returned with its taxYear, source URL and verification date. The figures change every April; every result names the tax year it applies to and carries cite.url, a databutler.dev permalink to the answer with its source.

tools.name: uk_rates_lookup
tools.title: UK rates lookup
tools.description: Current UK (2026-27) rates and thresholds, verified against gov.uk with source URLs and verification dates. Categories: income-tax, national-insurance, minimum-wage, student-loans, vat, isa, state-pension, state-pension-age, stamp-duty, capital-gains, pensions, dividends, savings, marriage-allowance, statutory-sick-pay, statutory-parental-pay, child-benefit. Covers UK income tax, National Insurance, minimum wage, student loans, VAT, ISAs, pensions, stamp duty, capital gains, dividends, savings, the State Pension and State Pension age, statutory sick/maternity/paternity pay and Child Benefit.

category.description: one of: income-tax, national-insurance, minimum-wage, student-loans, vat, isa, state-pension, state-pension-age, stamp-duty, capital-gains, pensions, dividends, savings, marriage-allowance, statutory-sick-pay, statutory-parental-pay, child-benefit (omit to list all)

mcp/uk-exams.instructions: UK exam-board specification data from databutler.dev, verified against official board pages. Built for student questions like "is electricity paper 2 AQA": exam_topic_paper returns which paper a topic is on in the current spec (boards move topics between specs), with the official spec source and cite.url, a databutler.dev permalink.

tools.name: exam_topic_paper
tools.title: Exam topic → paper
tools.description: Which exam paper is a topic on? The canonical student revision question ("is electricity paper 2 AQA?" — answer: no, Paper 1). Input a topic plus optional board/subject/level; returns the paper, sibling topics on that paper, spec code, and the official spec URL. Knows quirks like AQA Combined Science Trilogy Physics Paper 2 having no Space physics. Coverage: AQA GCSE Physics (8463); AQA GCSE Biology (8461); AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462); AQA GCSE Combined Science: Trilogy (8464); AQA GCSE Mathematics (8300).

topic.description: e.g. electricity, forces, ecology, organic chemistry

tools.name: exam_spec_lookup
tools.title: Exam spec lookup
tools.description: UK exam specification metadata: spec codes, paper structure (count, duration, marks, calculator rules, tiers), topic lists per paper, official spec links.

tools.name: exam_paper_index
tools.title: Exam past-paper index
tools.description: Official past-paper archive links per spec (links to the board's own assessment-resources page — papers are board copyright, so no hosted PDFs).

mcp/provenance.instructions: Live provenance signals for domains and software packages from databutler.dev — computed per request from RDAP, npm and PyPI. Returns, for an unfamiliar domain or package: age, registrar, maintainers, and typosquat resemblance to well-known names. These are DESCRIPTIVE SIGNALS, not verdicts: they do not establish that something is safe or phishing, and anything security-sensitive still needs checking through an independently trusted channel. Every result carries cite.url, a databutler.dev permalink.

tools.name: domain_provenance
tools.title: Domain provenance
tools.description: Who runs this domain? Live RDAP lookup: registration date and age, registrar, nameservers, status, whether the registrant is redacted, plus a typosquat check (edit-distance / brand-substring) against high-value brands. A very recently registered domain resembling a bank or big brand is a classic phishing signal — but report it as a signal, not a conclusion.

tools.name: package_provenance
tools.title: Package provenance
tools.description: Who publishes this package, and is it a typosquat? Live npm or PyPI lookup: first-publish date and age, release count, latest version, maintainers/author, linked repo, plus a typosquat check against popular package names. Use when an agent is about to install or recommend an unfamiliar dependency.

name.description: package name, e.g. express or requests

mcp/stats.instructions: Exact statistics and probability from databutler.dev: p-values, distribution tails, confidence intervals, Bayesian updates and regressions, computed numerically rather than estimated. The numerical core is validated against reference tables. Each result lists the assumptions it relies on and carries cite.url, a databutler.dev permalink.

tools.name: descriptive_stats
tools.title: Descriptive statistics
tools.description: Summary statistics for a numeric array: mean, median, sd, variance, quartiles, IQR, skewness, min/max.

tools.name: distribution
tools.title: Probability distribution
tools.description: Evaluate a probability distribution (normal, t, chi2, binomial, poisson): pdf/pmf and cdf at a value, and/or the quantile at a probability, plus mean & variance. Params per dist: normal {mean,sd}, t {df}, chi2 {df}, binomial {n,p}, poisson {lambda}.

at.description: value to evaluate pdf/pmf and cdf at

p.description: probability to get the quantile for (0-1)

tools.name: hypothesis_test
tools.title: Hypothesis test
tools.description: Run a significance test and get the statistic, p-value, and a plain-language interpretation with assumptions. test = one-sample-t {data, mu0}, two-sample-t {data1, data2}, one-proportion-z {successes, n, p0}, two-proportion-z {successes1,n1,successes2,n2}, chi2-gof {observed, expected?}, chi2-independence {table}. Optional tail: two-sided (default) | greater | less; alpha default 0.05.

tools.name: confidence_interval
tools.title: Confidence interval
tools.description: Confidence interval for a mean (t-based; from data, or n/mean/sd) or a proportion (Wilson; successes/n). kind = mean | proportion; confidence default 0.95.

tools.name: bayes_update
tools.title: Bayesian update
tools.description: Discrete Bayesian update: given competing hypotheses each with a prior and the likelihood of the observed evidence, return normalised posteriors. Priors are renormalised to sum to 1.

tools.name: linear_regression
tools.title: Linear regression
tools.description: Simple linear regression of y on x: slope, intercept, r, r², slope std error and p-value, equation.

mcp/vehicles.instructions: Official vehicle datasets from databutler.dev, one hub: UK MOT failure data (live from whatbreaks.uk — real DfT test outcomes), UK safety recalls (DVSA open data), French recalls (RappelConso / DGCCRF open data) and Japanese recalls + owner complaints (MLIT). Every result names its official source and verifiedDate; recall texts are the official English/French/Japanese originals — translate for the user but keep the recall/fiche/notification number and link. Counts are not reliability rankings (sales volume, multi-model campaigns). EU Safety Gate is a stub for now. Every result carries cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) and its official source.

tools.name: uk_mot_reliability
tools.title: UK MOT reliability
tools.description: Real UK MOT failure data for a used car: per-category failure rates (overall and interpolated at a given mileage) and the riskiest components with typical failure mileages, for one model generation. Live proxy to whatbreaks.uk (same operator; aggregated from DfT anonymised MOT results). Use when a user is buying, comparing or maintaining a car sold in the UK. If several generations match, the result lists candidates — retry with year or the exact model name.

model.description: e.g. Golf — generation resolved via year

tools.name: uk_mot_vehicle_search
tools.title: UK MOT vehicle search
tools.description: Search the 530 UK model generations covered by the MOT dataset by free text (e.g. "focus", "golf"). Use to check coverage or disambiguate a generation before uk_mot_reliability. Live proxy to whatbreaks.uk.

tools.name: uk_recalls_for_model
tools.title: UK recalls for a model
tools.description: Official UK vehicle safety recalls (DVSA, Open Government Licence; 4876 recalls launched 2016-01-01 → 2027-02-03, 272 makes) for a make and model: recall number, launch date, concern, defect and remedy text (DVSA's English originals), build-date range, vehicles affected and a GOV.UK recall-checker link. Omitting model lists the make's recalls and model names. "Vauxhall Corsa", "vauxhall corsa" and "VAUXHALL CORSA" resolve identically; "Mercedes-Benz", "VW" and "Land Rover" are understood. Covers cars, vans, HGVs, buses, motorcycles, trailers and components, not individual VINs.

make.description: e.g. Vauxhall, Mercedes-Benz, VW, Land Rover

model.description: e.g. Corsa, A Class, Golf (optional: omit to list the make)

since.description: optional ISO date YYYY-MM-DD — only recalls launched on/after it

tools.name: uk_recalls_search
tools.title: UK recalls search
tools.description: Keyword search across all served DVSA recalls (make, model names, concern, defect and remedy text), newest first, optionally since a date. Text is English ("airbag", "fire", "steering rack", "takata", "high voltage battery"); every word must appear. Suited to cross-make questions such as recent EV battery fire recalls in the UK.

text.description: words that must all appear, e.g. "airbag takata"

since.description: optional ISO date YYYY-MM-DD — only recalls launched on/after it

tools.name: fr_recalls_for_model
tools.title: French recalls for a model
tools.description: Official French vehicle recall notices (RappelConso, DGCCRF open data; 1663 automobile fiches 2018-01-19 → 2026-08-07) for a brand and model: fiche number, date, risks, defect description (motif, in French), commercialisation periods and the official fiche link. Omit model to list a brand. Matches by a reviewed alias table plus whole-word text match; each fiche says which.

model.description: e.g. 208, Classe A, Golf (optional: omit to list the brand)

tools.name: fr_recalls_search
tools.title: French recalls search
tools.description: Keyword search across all RappelConso automobile fiches (brand, model text, label, defect description, risks), newest first, optionally since a date. Text is French and lowercase ("airbag", "incendie", "takata", "batterie haute tension"). Use for cross-brand questions ("recent EV battery fire recalls in France").

text.description: words that must all appear, e.g. "airbag takata"

since.description: optional ISO date YYYY-MM-DD — only fiches published on/after it

tools.name: jp_recalls_for_model
tools.title: Japanese recalls for a model
tools.description: Official Japanese recall filings (国土交通省 MLIT; 3283 filings matched to 313 models sold in Japan, incl. Lexus and imports) for a make and model: notification number, date, defective device, affected vehicles, situation and remedy (Japanese originals) and the official filing PDF. Accepts English (Toyota Prius, Honda N-BOX) or Japanese (トヨタ プリウス) names.

model.description: e.g. prius, N-BOX, ジムニー

tools.name: jp_complaints_summary
tools.title: Japanese owner complaints summary
tools.description: Owner defect reports filed with MLIT's 不具合情報ホットライン (39954 across 313 models): total reports for a model and the breakdown by defective device (brakes, lights, engine, body…) from the newest sample. Reports are unverified owner submissions — compare shapes, not raw counts. Accepts English or Japanese names.

tools.name: eu_safety_gate_recalls
tools.title: EU Safety Gate recalls (stub)
tools.description: STUB — not yet live. EU Safety Gate (RAPEX) vehicle alerts are being added; until then this returns covered:false with the official Safety Gate URL and points to fr_recalls_* (RappelConso republishes the Safety Gate automobile alerts that concern France).

mcp/tax.instructions: Take-home pay from databutler.dev, computed live by the LifeByNumbers salary calculators (same operator) for uk, us, ca, au, in, br, pl, fr, de, es. take_home_pay applies the tax year's bracket thresholds, contribution ceilings and rebates, which move every year, and returns the taxYear, the assumptions list and the breakdown with the net figure: the result is a single-employee estimate under stated defaults (no voluntary pension, standard allowances), not personal tax advice. Spain returns covered:false (no upstream calculator). Every result carries cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) and the source calculator page.

tools.name: take_home_pay
tools.title: Take-home pay
tools.description: Net salary after income tax and social contributions for an employee in one of ten countries (uk, us, ca, au, in, br, pl, fr, de, es), computed live by the LifeByNumbers salary calculators (same operator). Takes a gross salary in local currency (annual by default, or monthly with period) and a country code, plus optional state and filingStatus for the US, province for Canada, region (england|scotland) for the UK. Returns gross, net and total deductions (each annual and monthly), a line-by-line breakdown typed as tax / social / contribution / repayment, effectiveRate, the tax year the figures apply to, currency, the assumptions behind the estimate and the upstream calculator page as source. Spain (es) is listed but answers covered:false because lifebynumbers.net computes it client-side only.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, lower case: uk, us, ca, au, in, br, pl, fr, de, es

gross.description: gross salary in local currency, annual unless period is monthly, e.g. 50000

period.description: period of gross (default annual); results always give both annual and monthly

state.description: US only: two-letter state code, e.g. TX (default CA)

province.description: Canada only: two-letter province/territory code, e.g. BC (default ON)

region.description: UK only: scotland applies Scottish income tax bands (default england)

mcp/software-eol.instructions: Software support lifecycles from databutler.dev: is this version still supported, and until when — for nodejs, python, ubuntu, debian, android, ios, macos, windows, oracle-jdk, go, ruby, php, postgresql, react. A committed monthly snapshot of endoflife.date open data (MIT), with the snapshot date on every answer (vendors move end-of-life dates every few months). support_status resolves a version string to its release cycle and states supported true/false with the eol date and days remaining or elapsed; support_timeline lists every cycle. Dates are as endoflife.date publishes them from vendor lifecycle pages; the recommendation is a plain statement, not advice about any one deployment. Every result carries cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) and the endoflife.date product page in source.

tools.name: support_status
tools.title: Software support status
tools.description: Whether a version of nodejs, python, ubuntu, debian, android, ios, macos, windows, oracle-jdk, go, ruby, php, postgresql, react is still supported, from a monthly snapshot of endoflife.date (340 release cycles, verified 2026-10-03). A version string resolves to its release cycle ("18", "18.19.0" and "v18" → Node.js 18; "3.11.4" → Python 3.11; "22.04.3" → Ubuntu 22.04; "bookworm" → Debian 12; "1.8.0_392" → Java 8; "11-24h2-w" → Windows 11 24H2 consumer). Returns supported true|false as of today, the eol date, days remaining or since end of life, active-support and extended-support end dates, LTS status, the latest release in the cycle, the newest supported (LTS) cycle, a plain-statement recommendation, and the endoflife.date page as source. "java" and "jdk" resolve to oracle-jdk; a version that fits several Windows editions comes back as candidates with each one's status; unknown products and versions answer with the nearest matches.

product.description: one of nodejs, python, ubuntu, debian, android, ios, macos, windows, oracle-jdk, go, ruby, php, postgresql, react (aliases: node, java, jdk, postgres, golang, osx, win)

version.description: a cycle ("18", "3.11", "22.04"), a full release ("18.19.0", "3.11.4"), a codename ("bookworm", "sonoma") or a Windows cycle id ("11-24h2-w")

tools.name: support_timeline
tools.title: Software support timeline
tools.description: Every release cycle of one of nodejs, python, ubuntu, debian, android, ios, macos, windows, oracle-jdk, go, ruby, php, postgresql, react, newest first, each with release date, supported true|false as of today, eol date, LTS status, latest release and active/extended-support end dates, plus the list of currently supported cycles and the newest supported LTS. From the same monthly endoflife.date snapshot as support_status, with the product page as source.

product.description: one of nodejs, python, ubuntu, debian, android, ios, macos, windows, oracle-jdk, go, ruby, php, postgresql, react (aliases accepted, e.g. node, java, postgres)

mcp/policy-rates.instructions: Current central-bank policy rates from databutler.dev — Bank of England Bank Rate, US Federal Reserve federal funds target range and the ECB key interest rates — each read from the bank's own page on verifiedDate, with effectiveFrom, decisionDate, the previous level and the next scheduled decision. These rates move up to eight times a year, so each policy_rate result says when the current level took effect and when it was last read from the bank. Present effectiveFrom and verifiedDate with the figure, and check nextDecision — a result whose nextDecision has passed may have been superseded, so say so. Other central banks are not covered (coverage lists them). Every result carries cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) and its official source.

tools.name: policy_rate
tools.title: Central-bank policy rate
tools.description: Current policy rate of one of three central banks, as published on the bank's own page: boe = Bank of England Bank Rate; fed = US Federal Reserve federal funds target range (lower and upper bound); ecb = European Central Bank deposit facility, main refinancing operations and marginal lending facility rates. Returns the figure(s) in % per annum, effectiveFrom, decisionDate and the meeting that set the level, the previous level with its effective date, the latest decision (which may be a hold), the next scheduled decision date, the official source page, the decision press release and verifiedDate. all: true returns every bank. Other central banks answer covered:false.

bank.description: boe | fed | ecb (common names such as "Bank of England", "FOMC" or "ECB" resolve too)

all.description: true returns every bank (bank may be omitted)

mcp/us-rates.instructions: Verified US federal rates and thresholds from databutler.dev — tax year 2026, each figure read from the IRS revenue procedure, IRS notice, SSA Federal Register notice or irs.gov page named in its source, with the quoted sentence or table row and verifiedDate. The IRS re-indexes most of these figures every October and November; us_rates_lookup returns the current tax year's values with the release each was read from. Present taxYear, source and verifiedDate with any figure; rate schedules are bracket rows (over, notOver, rate, taxAtLowerBound) exactly as the Rev. Proc. prints them, and each figure's previous block holds the prior-year value. Federal only — state income taxes, AMT, EITC and capital-gains brackets are not covered (coverage lists them). Every result carries cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) and its official source.

tools.name: us_rates_lookup
tools.title: US federal rates lookup
tools.description: Current US federal (tax year 2026) rates and thresholds read from the IRS revenue procedures and notices, SSA's Federal Register notice and irs.gov pages, each figure with its source URL, the quoted sentence or table row, verifiedDate and the prior-year value where one exists. Categories: income-tax (rate schedules for Single, Married filing jointly, Head of household and Married filing separately as bracket rows, standard deduction by filing status, additional and dependent standard deduction, top rate), social-security (OASDI wage base, employee and employer rates, COLA, quarter of coverage), medicare (rate, Additional Medicare Tax rate and thresholds by filing status, employer withholding threshold), retirement (401(k)/403(b)/457(b)/TSP deferral limit, age-50 and age-60–63 catch-ups, Roth catch-up wage threshold, § 415(c) and compensation limits, IRA and IRA catch-up, SIMPLE, highly compensated employee), hsa (contribution limits, HDHP minimum deductible and out-of-pocket maximum, excepted-benefit HRA), estate-gift (basic exclusion, GST exemption, annual gift exclusions). Federal only: state income taxes, AMT, EITC and capital-gains brackets are not covered. An unknown category answers covered:false with the nearest keys.

category.description: one of: income-tax, social-security, medicare, retirement, hsa, estate-gift (omit to list all)

mcp/de-rates.instructions: Verified German tax and social-insurance figures from databutler.dev — Veranlagungszeitraum 2026, each figure read from the consolidated statute on gesetze-im-internet.de, the Bundesgesetzblatt or the BMG/DRV/BMAS/Minijob-Zentrale page named in its source, with the German term, an English label, the quoted sentence and verifiedDate. The Beitragsbemessungsgrenzen, Bezugsgröße and Zusatzbeitrag move every January and the Grundfreibetrag, Kindergeld and Kinderfreibetrag with each Steuergesetz, so every de_rates_lookup figure names the year it applies to. Present taxYear, source and verifiedDate with any figure; social-insurance rates carry employeeShare and employerShare, and the Zusatzbeitrag served is the statutory average (each Krankenkasse sets its own). Figures already fixed for the following year (Mindestlohn, Geringfügigkeitsgrenze) carry their own effectiveFrom — present it. Kirchensteuer, Lohnsteuerklassen and Gewerbesteuer are not covered (coverage lists them). Every result carries cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) and its official source.

tools.name: de_rates_lookup
tools.title: German rates lookup
tools.description: Current German (Veranlagungszeitraum 2026) tax and social-insurance figures read from the consolidated statutes on gesetze-im-internet.de, the Bundesgesetzblatt and the BMG, DRV, BMAS, BMFSFJ and Minijob-Zentrale pages named in each figure's source — each with the German term and an English label, the quoted sentence, verifiedDate and the prior value where one exists. Categories: income-tax (Grundfreibetrag, § 32a tariff zones with their coefficients, Eingangssteuersatz, Spitzensteuersatz and Reichensteuer thresholds, Solidaritätszuschlag rate, Freigrenzen and Milderungszone), social-insurance (Beitragsbemessungsgrenzen RV/AV and KV/PV annual and monthly, Jahresarbeitsentgeltgrenze, Bezugsgröße, vorläufiges Durchschnittsentgelt, KV/RV/AV/PV Beitragssätze with employee and employer shares, durchschnittlicher Zusatzbeitrag, Kinderlosenzuschlag and Kinderabschlag, Sachsen split), minimum-wage (Mindestlohn 2026 and the fixed 2027 step), minijob (Geringfügigkeitsgrenze 2026 and 2027, Midijob upper limit), kindergeld, kinderfreibetrag (Kinderfreibetrag, BEA-Freibetrag, total per child), sparer-pauschbetrag, arbeitnehmer-pauschbetrag, entfernungspauschale. Federal law only: Kirchensteuer by Land, Lohnsteuerklassen mechanics and Gewerbesteuer are not covered, and 2027 draft figures are not served. An unknown category answers covered:false with the nearest keys.

category.description: one of: income-tax, social-insurance, minimum-wage, minijob, kindergeld, kinderfreibetrag, sparer-pauschbetrag, arbeitnehmer-pauschbetrag, entfernungspauschale (omit to list all)

mcp/uk-vehicle-rules.instructions: UK vehicle tax (VED) and MOT rules for 2026-27 from databutler.dev, each figure read from the gov.uk page in its source on verifiedDate with the table row or sentence it came from as quote and its 2025-26 value as previous. VED rates change every 1 April and the historic-vehicle exemption date rolls forward with them, so training-data figures for car tax are stale by the first April after the cutoff. Present the taxYear, the figure's unit and the source URL with any figure; a first-year rate depends on the CO2 band and on whether a diesel meets RDE2; the expensive car supplement threshold is £40,000 for most cars and £50,000 for zero-emission cars registered on or after 1 April 2025. MOT figures are Great Britain only; Northern Ireland, vans and HGV tax beyond the listed rows and company-car benefit in kind are not covered (coverage lists them). Every result carries cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) and its official source.

tools.name: uk_vehicle_rules_lookup
tools.title: UK vehicle tax (VED) & MOT rules
tools.description: UK vehicle tax (VED) and MOT rules for 2026-27, verified against gov.uk, by category: ved-first-year (first-year rate by CO2 band for cars registered on or after 1 April 2017, petrol/RDE2-diesel and other-diesel columns), ved-standard (the flat rate from the second year and the Direct Debit surcharges), ved-expensive-car (list price threshold, annual supplement, years applied), ved-2001-2017 (bands A–M), ved-pre-2001 (engine size), ved-electric (zero-emission cars taxable since 1 April 2025), historic (40-year MOT exemption and the vehicle-tax exemption build date), mot (first MOT at 3 years, maximum fees by class, early renewal, retests, exemptions) and penalties (no MOT, dangerous vehicle, untaxed vehicle). Each figure carries its value, unit, the quoted line from the page, its source URL, effectiveFrom and the previous year's value; the answer carries verifiedDate, freshness and a citation permalink. No category returns the listing; an unknown category answers covered:false with the nearest keys.

category.description: one of: ved-first-year, ved-standard, ved-expensive-car, ved-2001-2017, ved-pre-2001, ved-electric, historic, mot, penalties (omit to list all)

mcp/uk-exam-dates.instructions: UK exam dates from databutler.dev — results days, the summer exam timetable, entry deadlines and announced specification changes for GCSE and A-level (AQA, Pearson Edexcel, Cambridge OCR and WJEC/Eduqas; Scotland's results day), each read from the JCQ key-dates PDF, the board's own final timetable or fee document, or the regulator's announcement page named in its source, with the quoted row and verifiedDate. uk_exam_dates returns the current series' dates (the calendar moves every year): kind=results|timetable|deadlines|spec-changes, optional board and qualification. The timetable figures carry status (final) and, where the board still serves its 2026 document, the summer-2026 date as previous. Present the date with its board, document and verifiedDate; the JCQ dates apply to every JCQ board. Every result carries cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) and its official source.

tools.name: uk_exam_dates
tools.title: UK exam dates
tools.description: UK exam calendar dates verified against JCQ and the exam boards' own documents: results days (A-level 12 August 2027, GCSE 19 August 2027, November 2026 GCSE resits 13 January 2027, Scotland 10 August 2027), the summer 2027 exam timetable (JCQ common window 10 May – 22 June, contingency day 23 June 2027; per board — AQA, Pearson Edexcel, Cambridge OCR and WJEC/Eduqas, all final — the dates of GCSE Maths papers 1–3, English Language papers 1–2, Combined Science papers and A-level Maths papers), entry deadlines (JCQ 21 February 2027) with each board's late and very-late entry fee dates and multipliers, and announced specification changes (first-teaching and first-exam years, DfE reform timetable, Ofqual decisions). Input kind (results, timetable, deadlines, spec-changes; omitted → the listing), optional board (jcq, aqa, pearson/edexcel, ocr, wjec/eduqas, sqa, ofqual, dfe) and qualification (gcse, a-level). Every figure carries its source document, the quoted timetable row, verifiedDate (2026-10-04) and, where the board's 2026 document is still served, the summer-2026 date as previous. An unknown kind, board or qualification answers covered:false with the nearest keys.

kind.description: one of: results, timetable, deadlines, spec-changes (omit to list all)

board.description: optional: jcq (common dates), aqa, pearson (edexcel), ocr (cambridge), wjec-eduqas (wjec, eduqas), sqa (Scotland), ofqual, dfe

qualification.description: optional: gcse or a-level (figures common to both are returned for either)

mcp/calendar.instructions: Calendar facts from databutler.dev for 2026, 2027, 2028: public holidays (uk, us, de, fr), tax-year starts and ends (uk, us, au, in, ca, de, fr, br, pl) and daylight-saving switches (uk, de, fr, us, au, br; Brazil observes none). A committed monthly snapshot of the official lists (gov.uk bank-holidays.json, OPM's federal holiday tables, calendrier.api.gouv.fr, the German Länder statutes and ministry pages) and of statutes quoted sentence by sentence. calendar_facts answers one country and kind, with year and region optional; next_holiday gives the next public holiday after a date. Every answer carries source, verifiedDate and, where a fact could not be re-verified against an official page, nonOfficial: true with what was tried — present that flag when it is set. US federal holidays carry both the statutory date and OPM's observed date. Every result carries cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) and its official source.

tools.name: calendar_facts
tools.title: Calendar facts lookup
tools.description: Public holidays, tax-year dates or daylight-saving switches for one country in 2026–2028, from the official lists and statutes. kind=holidays (uk, us, de, fr): every public holiday of the year with its date and weekday, by region — UK nations (england-and-wales, scotland, northern-ireland; substitute days flagged), US federal (statutory date plus OPM's observed date when it falls on a weekend), German Länder by code or name (nationwide = the nine bundeseinheitlichen Feiertage; partial holidays carry their scope), French metropole or alsace-moselle. kind=tax-year (uk, us, au, in, ca, de, fr, br, pl): the personal tax year's start and end with the periods for 2026–2028 and the statute or official page quoted, plus the government fiscal year where it differs. kind=dst (uk, de, fr, us, au, br): the statutory rule and the computed clocks-forward and clocks-back dates per year, with the states that observe it for Australia and observed:false for Brazil. Country names, UK nations, German Land names (Bavaria, Sachsen) and kind synonyms (bank holidays, financial year, clocks) resolve; no country lists everything covered; unknown countries, regions and years answer covered:false with the nearest matches. Entries that could not be re-verified against an official page carry nonOfficial: true.

country.description: one of uk, us, de, fr, au, in, ca, br, pl, or a name (United Kingdom, Germany, Bavaria resolves to de with region BY); omit to list

kind.description: holidays | tax-year | dst (synonyms accepted: bank holidays, financial year, daylight saving)

year.description: 2026–2028; holidays default to the current year, tax-year and dst to all years covered

region.description: UK: england-and-wales | scotland | northern-ireland; US: federal; Germany: nationwide or a Land (BY, Bayern, Bavaria, …); France: metropole | alsace-moselle

tools.name: next_holiday

The data runs to the end of 2028; a later date answers covered:false with the last date covered. From the same monthly snapshot of the official lists, with the list's URL as source.

country.description: one of uk, us, de, fr, or a name

from.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD; the next holiday is the first one after this day (default: today)

mcp/uk-gov-process.instructions: Current UK government service facts from databutler.dev — passports (UK and overseas fees), driving licence renewal (10-year photocard, 70 and over), provisional licences, change of address (licence and V5C), vehicle tax and SORN, register to vote, birth and death registration (England and Wales), Blue Badge, Self Assessment registration and deadlines (with Making Tax Digital for Income Tax), National Insurance numbers, Universal Credit basics, the EU Settlement Scheme, eVisas (BRPs replaced) and the electronic travel authorisation (ETA). Each figure was read from the gov.uk page in its source on verifiedDate with the sentence it came from as quote; each service carries its official startUrl and a dated changes list. Fees here moved in 2025 and 2026 (passports 8 April 2026, ETA £20 from 8 April 2026, Universal Credit 2-child limit ended 6 April 2026), so training-data figures are often stale. Present the fee, the verifiedDate and the source or startUrl together. Scotland- and Northern Ireland-specific variants, local-council services and immigration routes beyond the EU Settlement Scheme, eVisa and ETA are not covered (coverage lists them). Every result carries cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) and its official source.

mcp/jp-vehicle-costs.instructions: Japan vehicle statutory costs from databutler.dev — the 法定費用 of a 車検 (自動車重量税, 自賠責保険, 検査手数料) and the annual 自動車税 and 軽自動車税 — each figure read from the MLIT, FSA, NALTEC, 総務省, Tokyo Metropolitan Tax Bureau or Kōtō City page in its source on verifiedDate, with the table row it came from as quote and the Japanese term as term. Several of these change on fixed dates: the 自賠責 rates for policies starting on or after 2026-11-01 are the keys ending -from-2026-11 (the current-table figures carry effectiveTo 2026-10-31); the weight-tax table runs 2026-05-01 to 2028-04-30; inspection fees rose on 2026-04-01 (previous carries the old amount). Registered-car weight tax is per 0.5 t of vehicle weight, rounded up; kei weight tax is flat. Car taxes are the standard rates as levied by Tokyo and Kōtō City. Every result carries verifiedDate, freshness and cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) beside the official source.

Each figure carries its value in JPY, unit, the Japanese term, the quoted row from the page, its source URL and effectiveFrom (and effectiveTo where the source states an end); the answer carries verifiedDate, freshness and a citation permalink. mcp/jp-living-costs.instructions: Japan daily-life official figures from databutler.dev — 地域別最低賃金 by prefecture, 協会けんぽ health insurance rates by prefecture with 介護保険料率 and 子ども・子育て支援金率, 厚生年金保険料率, 国民年金保険料, 老齢基礎年金 満額, 雇用保険料率, 児童手当, 出産育児一時金, 高額療養費, the 2027 national holidays, 消費税 rates, 所得税 基礎控除 / 給与所得控除 and 住民税 均等割 — each read from the MHLW, NTA, 総務省, 内閣府, こども家庭庁, 日本年金機構 or 協会けんぽ page in its source on verifiedDate, with the row it came from as quote and the Japanese term as term. The FY2026 minimum wages take effect on a different day in each prefecture (2026-10-01 to 2026-12-02): before a figure's effectiveFrom, its previous (FY2025) amount still applies. Health insurance rates are employer + employee combined and apply to 協会けんぽ members only. The 2026 deduction amounts take effect from 2026-12-01 for the 2026 tax year. Every result carries verifiedDate, freshness and cite.url (a databutler.dev permalink) beside the official source.

mcp/facts.instructions: Verified Facts from databutler.dev (protocol verified-facts/0.2): one official figure per key — UK, US and German tax and social-insurance thresholds and rates, UK vehicle tax and MOT rules, UK government service fees, UK exam dates and central-bank policy rates — each with value, period, effectiveFrom, the official source, verifiedDate, a content hash and an Ed25519 signature. For any official figure, get_fact with the key you would guess and the max_age the question deserves (a tax calculation: 30d) answers in one call; a miss lists candidate keys, and resolve_fact finds a key from a question. Present value with period, say verifiedDate and quote source; when status is stale, say the verification is older than asked. what_changed_since lists what moved after a date, each entry with its factKey. Every result carries cite.url, a permalink to the figure with its source.

tools.name: get_fact
tools.title: Get a verified fact
tools.description: The current value of one official figure by key — a tax threshold, rate, allowance, fee, deadline, limit or policy rate — with the date it was verified, the official source URL, the period it applies to and a signature. Keys are `<country>/<topic>/<fact>`, e.g. `uk/income-tax/personal-allowance`, `uk/national-insurance/primary-threshold`, `us/social-security/wage-base`, `de/income-tax/grundfreibetrag`, `uk/bank-rate`, `eu/ecb/deposit-facility`, `uk/gov/passport-renewal-adult/fee-online-uk`. A loose key is resolved when unambiguous; otherwise the answer lists candidate keys. `max_age` (e.g. `30d`) marks the answer `stale` when the verification is older than that. Several keys separated by commas return a batch. Covers UK, US and German rates and thresholds, UK vehicle tax and MOT rules, UK government service fees, UK exam dates and central-bank policy rates; `coverage` lists the rest.

key.description: one key, or several separated by commas (max 50), e.g. uk/income-tax/personal-allowance

as_of.description: optional YYYY-MM-DD: the value in force that day

period.description: optional period label instead of as_of, e.g. 2025-26

tools.name: resolve_fact
tools.title: Find the key for a fact
tools.description: Ranked canonical fact keys for a plain-language question or a guessed key — "NI primary threshold", "ECB deposit rate", "passport renewal fee" — each with label, unit, period and verification date, and the full record of the top match when it is unambiguous. The keys feed `get_fact`. Filter by `namespace` (`uk`, `us`, `de`, `eu`).

annotations.title: Find the key for a fact

mcp.instructions: Data Butler (databutler.dev): official reference figures, each returned with its official source URL and the date a person verified it against that source. get_fact returns one figure by key — a threshold, rate, allowance, fee or deadline — with value, period, effectiveFrom, source, verifiedDate, a fresh/stale flag and an Ed25519 signature; resolve_fact turns a plain-language question into a key. what_changed_since returns every verified figure that changed after a given date (UK, US and German tax thresholds, policy rates, exam-spec facts), with before and after values, the effective date and the Budget or spec change behind each. uk_rates_lookup returns the current UK tax-year rates and thresholds verified against gov.uk. take_home_pay returns net pay computed live by the LifeByNumbers calculators for us, uk, ca, au, in, br, de, fr and pl, with its taxYear and assumptions. coverage returns exactly what each area covers and does not. The tools listed here are the high-frequency set; catalogue lists every tool on every Data Butler server (UK rates; UK exams; provenance; exact statistics; vehicles: UK MOT, UK, French and Japanese recalls; take-home pay for ten countries; software support status and end-of-life timelines for 14 runtimes and operating systems; central-bank policy rates: Bank of England, Fed, ECB; US federal rates and thresholds (us_rates_lookup: income tax, Social Security, Medicare, retirement, HSA, estate and gift); German tax and social-insurance figures (de_rates_lookup: Einkommensteuertarif, Sozialversicherung, Mindestlohn, Minijob, Kindergeld, Kinderfreibetrag, Pauschbeträge, Entfernungspauschale); UK vehicle tax (VED) and MOT rules; UK exam dates and spec changes: results days, the summer 2027 timetable, entry deadlines, new specifications; calendar facts: public holidays, tax-year starts and daylight-saving switches for 2026–2028; UK government services: passport, driving licence, vehicle tax/SORN, voting, birth/death registration, Blue Badge, Self Assessment, NI number, Universal Credit, EU Settlement Scheme, eVisa, ETA; Japan vehicle statutory costs (jp_vehicle_costs_lookup: 自動車重量税, エコカー減税, 自賠責保険, 検査手数料, 自動車税, 軽自動車税); Japan daily-life official figures (jp_living_costs_lookup: 最低賃金, 健康保険料率, 年金, 雇用保険, 児童手当, 高額療養費, 祝日, 消費税, 基礎控除, 住民税)) and call runs any of them by name. policy_rate returns the current Bank of England, Fed and ECB policy rates, each read from the bank's own page, with effectiveFrom, verifiedDate and the next scheduled decision. US federal figures (IRS brackets and standard deduction, Social Security wage base, 401(k)/IRA/HSA limits, estate and gift exclusions) are returned by us_rates_lookup (via call), each read from the IRS or SSA release with verifiedDate. German figures (Grundfreibetrag and tariff, Beitragsbemessungsgrenzen and Beitragssätze, Mindestlohn, Minijob limit, Kindergeld, Pauschbeträge) are returned by de_rates_lookup (via call), each read from the statute or ministry page with verifiedDate. Every result carries freshness (verifiedDate, staleness) and cite.url, a permalink a human can open to see the answer with its official source.

tools.name: domain_provenance
tools.title: Domain provenance
tools.description: Who runs this domain? Live RDAP lookup: registration date and age, registrar, nameservers, status, whether the registrant is redacted, plus a typosquat check (edit-distance / brand-substring) against high-value brands. A very recently registered domain resembling a bank or big brand is a classic phishing signal — but report it as a signal, not a conclusion.

tools.description: Who publishes this package, and is it a typosquat? Live npm or PyPI lookup: first-publish date and age, release count, latest version, maintainers/author, linked repo, plus a typosquat check against popular package names. Use when an agent is about to install or recommend an unfamiliar dependency.

tools.name: take_home_pay
tools.title: Take-home pay
tools.description: Net salary after income tax and social contributions for an employee in one of ten countries (uk, us, ca, au, in, br, pl, fr, de, es), computed live by the LifeByNumbers salary calculators (same operator). Takes a gross salary in local currency (annual by default, or monthly with period) and a country code, plus optional state and filingStatus for the US, province for Canada, region (england|scotland) for the UK. Returns gross, net and total deductions (each annual and monthly), a line-by-line breakdown typed as tax / social / contribution / repayment, effectiveRate, the tax year the figures apply to, currency, the assumptions behind the estimate and the upstream calculator page as source. Spain (es) is listed but answers covered:false because lifebynumbers.net computes it client-side only.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, lower case: uk, us, ca, au, in, br, pl, fr, de, es

gross.description: gross salary in local currency, annual unless period is monthly, e.g. 50000

period.description: period of gross (default annual); results always give both annual and monthly

state.description: US only: two-letter state code, e.g. TX (default CA)

province.description: Canada only: two-letter province/territory code, e.g. BC (default ON)

region.description: UK only: scotland applies Scottish income tax bands (default england)

tools.description: Every tool across all Data Butler servers (UK rates; UK exams; provenance; exact statistics; vehicles: UK MOT, UK, French and Japanese recalls; take-home pay for ten countries; software support status and end-of-life timelines for 14 runtimes and operating systems; central-bank policy rates: Bank of England, Fed, ECB; US federal rates and thresholds (us_rates_lookup: income tax, Social Security, Medicare, retirement, HSA, estate and gift); German tax and social-insurance figures (de_rates_lookup: Einkommensteuertarif, Sozialversicherung, Mindestlohn, Minijob, Kindergeld, Kinderfreibetrag, Pauschbeträge, Entfernungspauschale); UK vehicle tax (VED) and MOT rules; UK exam dates and spec changes: results days, the summer 2027 timetable, entry deadlines, new specifications; calendar facts: public holidays, tax-year starts and daylight-saving switches for 2026–2028; UK government services: passport, driving licence, vehicle tax/SORN, voting, birth/death registration, Blue Badge, Self Assessment, NI number, Universal Credit, EU Settlement Scheme, eVisa, ETA; Japan vehicle statutory costs (jp_vehicle_costs_lookup: 自動車重量税, エコカー減税, 自賠責保険, 検査手数料, 自動車税, 軽自動車税); Japan daily-life official figures (jp_living_costs_lookup: 最低賃金, 健康保険料率, 年金, 雇用保険, 児童手当, 高額療養費, 祝日, 消費税, 基礎控除, 住民税)), with input schemas — including tools not listed at this front door. Optional query filters by keyword. Run any of them with call, or connect to serverUrl directly.

query.description: keyword filter, e.g. regression, exam, npm

tools.name: call
tools.title: Call any tool
tools.description: Run any Data Butler tool by name — the long tail not listed here: exam_spec_lookup, exam_paper_index; exact statistics (distribution, hypothesis_test, confidence_interval, bayes_update, linear_regression, descriptive_stats); the vehicles hub (uk_mot_reliability, uk_recalls_for_model, uk_recalls_search, fr_recalls_for_model, fr_recalls_search, jp_recalls_for_model, jp_complaints_summary); software end-of-life (support_status {product, version}, support_timeline {product} for nodejs, python, ubuntu, debian, android, ios, macos, windows, oracle-jdk, go, ruby, php, postgresql, react); policy_rate (Bank of England Bank Rate, Fed federal funds target range, ECB key rates — committed data verified against the banks' own pages); us_rates_lookup (US federal rates and thresholds for the current tax year: income-tax, social-security, medicare, retirement, hsa, estate-gift); de_rates_lookup (German tax and social-insurance figures for the current Veranlagungszeitraum: income-tax, social-insurance, minimum-wage, minijob, kindergeld, kinderfreibetrag, sparer-pauschbetrag, arbeitnehmer-pauschbetrag, entfernungspauschale); uk_vehicle_rules_lookup (UK car tax: first-year CO2 bands, standard rate, expensive car supplement, 2001–2017 bands, pre-2001 rates, electric cars, historic vehicles; MOT due dates, fees, retests, penalties — verified against gov.uk); UK exam dates (uk_exam_dates {kind: results|timetable|deadlines|spec-changes, board?, qualification?}); calendar facts (calendar_facts {country, kind: holidays|tax-year|dst, year?, region?} and next_holiday {country, from?} — holidays for uk, us, de, fr; tax years and DST for uk, us, de, fr, au, in, ca, br, pl; 2026–2028); uk_gov_process (UK government services — passport and ETA fees, driving licence renewal, SORN, register to vote, birth/death registration, Self Assessment deadlines, NI number, Universal Credit, EU Settlement Scheme, eVisa — fees, processing times, start URLs, dated changes, verified against gov.uk); jp_vehicle_costs_lookup (Japan 車検 statutory costs and car taxes: weight-tax, weight-tax-eco, cali, inspection-fee, auto-tax, kei-tax — verified against MLIT, FSA, NALTEC and local-government pages); jp_living_costs_lookup (Japan minimum wage by prefecture, 協会けんぽ rates, pensions, employment insurance, benefits, 2027 holidays, consumption tax, income-tax deductions, resident tax — verified against MHLW, NTA, 総務省, 内閣府, こども家庭庁, 日本年金機構 and 協会けんぽ pages). uk_rates_lookup, domain_provenance, package_provenance and take_home_pay are listed directly. See catalogue for schemas. The result carries the inner tool's freshness and cite.
